findings.title: The duration is disclosed, not independently reproduced
findings.claim: The focus presents the disputed stay as a count whose warrant belongs to divine knowledge: the numeral may be stated, while creaturely estimation, conjecture, and dispute do not become an independent route to the elapsed interval.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms for remaining and knowing meet the pericope's exhaustive reckoning, the sleepers' day-level estimate, conjectural counting into the unseen, and the precise hundred-plus-nine immediately before 18:26. That sequence makes the focus audit the provenance of the duration rather than merely repeat that God knows it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the exact number and the refusal of autonomous access stand together: the passage gives a count while withholding creaturely ownership of its warrant.
findings.containment: This preserves the ordinary declaration that God knows the stay and does not adjudicate or retract the stated duration. The count-provenance relation is an attributed macro reading from the supplied HFT trace, not an independent reconstruction of chronology.

epistemic.reason: All five anchor ayat and their Arabic surfaces are supplied, but the analytic branch roles and cross-ayah mechanism remain legacy_unbound HFT nominations.

findings.title: Access can be closed, misread, and opened
findings.claim: The focus's exclamations of divine seeing and hearing also close a pericope demonstration that creaturely access can be sealed, misdirected, or opened, while divine apprehension remains continuous and governs when hidden reality becomes knowable.
findings.mechanism: The ears are put out of reception, visible bodies appear awake while sleeping, attempted inspection produces fear rather than understanding, and later discovery makes the hidden sleepers knowable. These distinct sensory events return through the focus's seeing, hearing, and hidden-domain words.
findings.reader_payoff: The praise of divine perception gains a narrative contrast: the reader can recognize that human channels are present but not self-authorizing, and that access changes under divine governance.
findings.containment: The finding retains the ordinary exclamatory praise of God's perfect seeing and hearing. It does not claim that human perception is always false or that the focus reduces to a general epistemology; the controlled-access sequence is attributed to the supplied pericope trace.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic anchor surfaces and all four in-pericope anchors are present, but the cross-ayah sensory mechanism is a legacy_unbound HFT nomination.

findings.title: Planning does not become an independent decree
findings.claim: The focus's denial of partnership in divine judgment also reaches the executability of human plans: intention and action remain real, but no speaker can turn a future plan into an independently binding decree alongside God's effective judgment.
findings.mechanism: The immediately preceding verses restrain categorical speech about tomorrow, condition the planned act by divine willing, and then the focus denies any co-participant in God's judgment. Speech, action, future interval, willing, judgment, and exhaustive negation therefore contact one another as a single limit on independent future control.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the final clause as touching the practical future just described, not only a remote courtroom sense of judgment.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that God admits no partner in His judgment remains primary, and the narrower judicial reading remains live. The extension to effective determination is an attributed contextual relation, not a denial of human action or intention.

epistemic.reason: The adjacent future speech, divine-will condition, and focus judgment clause are supplied exactly; the extension from judicial judgment to executability is a legacy_unbound HFT inference.
